title: Plural partitive in existence statements
summary: In a location-first statement, use plural partitive for an unspecified collection: Pöydällä on kirjoja. — There are books on the table. Keep on (“there are”) or ei ole (“there are no”) in this pattern, even though the noun is plural.
objectives: Use plural partitive when introducing an unspecified collection at a location or denying its presence.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Use plural partitive when introducing an unspecified collection at a location or denying its presence.
The location-first pattern uses on even though the collection is plural. Ei ole denies its presence. These verb frames are supplied; choose the noun form for the stated collection.
A statement about an already identified complete set is a different construction. This lesson introduces or denies an open collection.
keyPoints: In this location-first existence pattern, an unspecified collection uses plural partitive; the verb frame remains on or ei ole.

examples.english: There are books on the table.
steps: In this location-first existence pattern, an unspecified collection uses plural partitive; the verb frame remains on or ei ole.
Pöydällä means “on the table” and works as the location. pöytä uses the weak stem pöydä- (t → d) plus -llä: pöydällä.
on means “is / there is / there are” and works as the verb. on comes from olla: the present third-person singular form on.
kirjoja means “books” and works as the plural partitive noun naming the present or absent item. Replace final a with o, then add -ja: kirjo- + -ja = kirjoja.

examples.english: There are toys in the box.
steps: In this location-first existence pattern, an unspecified collection uses plural partitive; the verb frame remains on or ei ole.
Laatikossa means “in the box” and works as the location. laatikko uses the weak stem laatiko- (kk → k) plus -ssa: laatikossa.
on means “is / there is / there are” and works as the verb. on comes from olla: the present third-person singular form on.
leluja means “toys” and works as the plural partitive noun naming the present or absent item. Keep lelu and add -ja: lelu + ja = leluja.

examples.english: There are cups on the shelf.
steps: In this location-first existence pattern, an unspecified collection uses plural partitive; the verb frame remains on or ei ole.
Hyllyllä means “on the shelf” and works as the location. hylly + -llä = hyllyllä; front vowels choose -llä.
on means “is / there is / there are” and works as the verb. on comes from olla: the present third-person singular form on.
kuppeja means “cups” and works as the plural partitive noun naming the present or absent item. Change final i to e and keep strong pp: kuppe- + -ja = kuppeja.

examples.english: There are balls in the box.
steps: In this location-first existence pattern, an unspecified collection uses plural partitive; the verb frame remains on or ei ole.
Laatikossa means “in the box” and works as the location. laatikko uses the weak stem laatiko- (kk → k) plus -ssa: laatikossa.
on means “is / there is / there are” and works as the verb. on comes from olla: the present third-person singular form on.
palloja means “balls” and works as the plural partitive noun naming the present or absent item. Keep pallo and add -ja: pallo + ja = palloja.

commonMistakes: Do not substitute a plural nominative for an unspecified collection here.
Keep the provided on or ei ole frame; the noun’s plural form does not require a plural verb here.
